title: Associated localizations of a fractional monogenic algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $K$ its fraction field, and $x\in K$ nonzero. Assume $S=R[x]$ is Noetherian, and let $m$ be a maximal ideal of $S$ containing $x$. Put $A=S_m$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $t=x/1$. For every associated prime $p$ of $A/tA$, there exists a prime $q$ of $R$ of height one and a ring isomorphism $A_p\cong R_q$.

source.place: Tag 0334, Step 5, paragraphs identifying S/xS = R/(R ∩ xR) and verifying (2), (3)(a); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0334

proof.text: Contract p to qS in S and then q in R. The associated-contraction theorem gives that q is associated to R/(R ∩ xR). The height part of Tag 031T gives q.height = 1.

Normality localizes. Thus B = R_q is a one-dimensional Noetherian normal local domain, hence a regular local DVR. The canonical localization map f : B → C = S_qS is local, since q is the contraction of qS.

Identify K with Frac(R). The inclusion S → Frac(R) is injective and sends every element outside qS to a nonzero element. Extend it to an injective map g : C → Frac(R). Localization extensionality gives g composed with f equal to the fraction-field inclusion of B.

Apply Mathlib bijective_rangeRestrict_comp_of_valuationRing to the local map f and the fraction-field embedding g. It gives a bijection from B to the range of g. Injectivity of g gives that f itself is bijective, hence B ≃ C.

Iterated localization identifies A_p with S_qS, since qS is the contraction of p. Compose this equivalence with C ≃ B. All objects and maps are explicit; no arbitrary witness is chosen from an unproved existence theorem.
